memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 should prioritize electrification, reliability, grid hardware, transformer/power-quality equipment, HVDC/FACTS, and nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks rather than treating Energy as only oil/gas, utilities, uranium mining, or SMR narratives.

Transmission-line hardware remains the cleanest underfollowed node because utility-qualified fittings, dampers, spacers, connectors, pole-line hardware, and related line accessories may have specification lock-in and limited analyst attention.

Transformers, dry-type transformers, magnetics, switchgear, power distribution, and power-quality products are central energy chokepoints for AI data centers, industrial electrification, renewables, utilities, microgrids, and aging-grid replacement.

HVDC, FACTS, reactors, harmonic filters, STATCOM, and high-voltage power-quality components deserve a dedicated global supplier search because qualification cycles, reliability requirements, and limited supplier pools can create bottleneck economics.
Nuclear fuel-cycle middle steps, especially conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and fabrication, should be separated from uranium mining and SMR developer narratives in later layers.

Next layer must validate candidates with primary filings, segment revenue, backlog, margin trend, certifications, approved-vendor evidence, customer evidence, market cap, liquidity, analyst coverage, and valuation before any investability ranking.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for Energy prioritizes electrification, grid reliability, physical T&D bottlenecks, transformer and power-quality equipment, HVDC/FACTS components, and nuclear fuel-cycle middle steps. The highest Serenity relevance is concentrated in certified, specification-bound, hard-to-substitute suppliers rather than the most visible utilities, hyperscalers, miners, or mega-cap OEMs. The universe intentionally balances reference leaders used for context with underfollowed small/mid-cap or niche second-order names that may sit closer to chokepoints but require primary-source validation in later layers.
